lines.keys: bid extracted as trailing digits of book_id ('bookid_N'->N) joined to bid extracted from purchase_id ('purchaseid_N'->N); exact integer match.
lines.rank: Order decades by avg_rating descending, no explicit tie-break specified, limit to 1 row.
lines.parse: Regex extracts the year following the first month name (optionally with day and comma) in details; if absent, same pattern applied to subtitle as fallback; result cast to int as pub_year.
lines.shape: Single column 'decade', one row, the decade value as an integer (e.g. representing a decade like 1980).
lines.filter: Rows require a non-null pub_year (books with no month-anchored date, i.e. no match in details or subtitle, are dropped); after grouping, only decades with n_books >= 10 are kept.
lines.metric: Grouped by decade computed as (pub_year/10)*10; metric is avg(rating) across all joined review rows per decade, plus count(distinct bid) as n_books for the filter.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info.details (templated prose with publication date) and .subtitle (fallback date text) for pub year; bookreview_review.rating for ratings; book_id/purchase_id hold row identifiers.

lines.keys: book_id 'bookid_N' and purchase_id 'purchaseid_N' are matched by extracting the trailing integer N from each with a regex and casting to int.
lines.rank: no explicit tie-break needed since filtering to avg=5; results are ordered alphabetically by title with no row limit.
lines.parse: categories is matched by looking for the literal quoted substring "Literature & Fiction" in the string; language is detected by a word-boundary regex match for 'English' anywhere in the details text.
lines.shape: single column named title, one row per matching book, with titles containing a comma wrapped in double quotes (CSV-style escaping) and internal quotes doubled.
lines.filter: keep rows where categories contains the quoted 'Literature & Fiction' element, details matches the English word-boundary pattern, and the book's average rating across its reviews equals exactly 5.
lines.metric: average rating per book computed by grouping bookreview_review rows by the extracted book id and taking avg(rating) over individual review rows.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info holds book_id, title, categories (JSON-like string list) and details (templated prose text); bookreview_review holds purchase_id and rating.

lines.keys: trailing digits after 'bookid_' in book_id match trailing digits after 'purchaseid_' in purchase_id, both cast to int.
lines.rank: order by average rating descending, then title ascending; no row limit.
lines.parse: review_time text cast to timestamp for comparison; categories matched via regex for the quoted literal "Children's Books" within the string list.
lines.shape: single column of title, CSV-quoted (wrapped in double quotes, internal quotes doubled) if it contains a comma, one row per qualifying book.
lines.filter: reviews with review_time::timestamp >= 2020-01-01; books whose categories string contains the quoted "Children's Books" element; only average ratings >= … kept.
lines.metric: average rating per book_id (via matched purchase_id trailing number) computed over qualifying reviews, one row per book.
lines.sources: bookreview_books_info gives book_id, title, categories (string-encoded list); bookreview_review gives purchase_id, rating, review_time (text timestamp).

lines.keys: voicecalltranscript__c.LeadId__c joined to lead.Id after stripping leading '#' and trimming on both sides; pricebookentry.Product2Id stripped of '#' matched to product2.Id similarly stripped
lines.rank: calls ordered newest first by CreatedDate via row_number; products ordered alphabetically; policy rules ordered by their paragraph number; final union ordered by source group then that order
lines.parse: product names matched by substring position in call body text; knowledge faq_answer__c split into numbered paragraphs on blank lines, keeping only paragraphs starting with 'digit.'
lines.shape: single result set with columns kind, ref_id, label, detail, listing one lead row, then call rows, then price rows, then policy rule rows, no aggregation or dedupe of BANT verdict
lines.filter: lead restricted to the given lead_id; products kept only if their trimmed name appears somewhere in a call body; knowledge articles kept where summary equals title and title matches Budget/Authority/Need/Timeline as whole words
lines.metric: no aggregation; each row is an individual evidence item (lead record, one call, one product price, one policy rule) at its own grain
lines.sources: crmarenapro_lead for lead fields; crmarenapro_voicecalltranscript__c.Body__c for call text; crmarenapro_product2/pricebookentry for UnitPrice; crmarenapro_knowledge__kav.faq_answer__c for policy rule text

lines.keys: cases join assignments on case id after stripping leading '#'/whitespace from case.id and casehistory caseid__c and newvalue__c/ownerid; handled agents = union of assignment agent_id and case owner_id per case.
lines.rank: order by average handle time ascending, tie-broken by agent_id ascending, limit to 1 row.
lines.parse: trim(field__c) matched exactly to literal 'Owner Assignment' to identify assignment rows; newvalue__c stripped of leading '#' and whitespace gives agent id; dates cast directly from ISO timestamptz strings.
lines.shape: single column agent_id, one row, the agent with lowest average handle time.
lines.filter: case createddate within [today-4 months, today+1 day); handle_times only for cases with closed_at not null and exactly one Owner Assignment row (untransferred); eligible agents need >1 distinct handled case (owner or any assignment).
lines.metric: handle time in seconds = closed_at - opened_at extracted as epoch, computed per untransferred closed case, credited to case owner; averaged per agent_id.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case gives case id, ownerid, createddate, closeddate; crmarenapro_casehistory__c gives caseid__c, field__c and newvalue__c holding owner-assignment agent ids.

lines.keys: Contact.AccountId links to Order.AccountId; Order.Id links to OrderItem.OrderId; OrderItem.Product2Id links to Product2.Id; all Id/AccountId values trimmed and stripped of leading '#' before matching.
lines.rank: No ordering, tie-break, or limit applied; DISTINCT is used to dedupe identical product ids.
lines.parse: EffectiveDate is read as text then trimmed and cast to date (format 'YYYY-MM-DD'); no JSON parsing involved.
lines.shape: Single column output: product_id (the normalised Product2 Id), potentially multiple rows though expected to be one.
lines.filter: Contact.Id equals the given contact id (after normalising); order EffectiveDate falls within the previous calendar month relative to today (2021-07-15, i.e. June 2021); product Name matches 'AI' as a whole word via regex.
lines.metric: No aggregation; simply selects distinct matching product rows at the grain of one row per qualifying product id.
lines.sources: Tables: crmarenapro_contact (Id, AccountId), crmarenapro_order (Id, AccountId, EffectiveDate text), crmarenapro_orderitem (OrderId, Product2Id), crmarenapro_product2 (Id, Name).

lines.keys: Join Opportunity.ContractID__c to Contract.Id as an exact key, after trimming whitespace and stripping leading '#' from both sides.
lines.rank: Order agents by ascending average cycle days, tie-broken alphabetically by agent id, take the top row.
lines.parse: CreatedDate's first 10 characters cast to date for opportunity creation; CompanySignedDate cast directly to date (plain YYYY-MM-DD).
lines.shape: Single row, single column named Id, containing the winning agent's identifier.
lines.filter: Keep only rows where Contract.CompanySignedDate falls within April 2023 (>= 2023-04-01 and < 2023-05-01).
lines.metric: For each agent (trimmed, '#'-stripped OwnerId), compute average of (CompanySignedDate - CreatedDate) in days across their matched opportunities.
lines.sources: Opportunity table gives OwnerId (agent) and CreatedDate; Contract table gives Id and CompanySignedDate; link via Opportunity.ContractID__c.

lines.keys: Orders join contracts on AccountId equality and order.EffectiveDate = contract.StartDate (both trimmed/stripped of '#' and whitespace); orderitem joins orders on OrderId = order.Id after same normalisation.
lines.rank: Order agents by sales_amount descending, tie-break by agent_id ascending, and take only the top row.
lines.parse: Ids are cleaned by trimming whitespace and stripping leading '#' via ltrim/trim; date strings like CompanySignedDate, StartDate, EffectiveDate are cast to date using 'YYYY-MM-DD' format; Quantity and UnitPrice text fields are cast to numeric.
lines.shape: Return a single column, single row containing just the agent_id (the top agent's Id).
lines.filter: Keep contracts whose CompanySignedDate falls between today (2022-11-25) minus 5 months and today inclusive; keep orders that match at least one such contract via the account/start-date join; distinct order rows to avoid duplicate matches from multiple contracts.
lines.metric: For each agent (order OwnerId), sum Quantity*UnitPrice across all their matched orders' order items to get total sales_amount, grouped by agent_id.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_contract holds AccountId, StartDate, CompanySignedDate; crmarenapro_order holds Id, OwnerId (agent), AccountId, EffectiveDate; crmarenapro_orderitem holds OrderId, Quantity, UnitPrice (all as text fields).

lines.keys: QuoteId, Product2Id, PricebookEntryId are matched to Id columns after trimming whitespace and stripping a leading '#' with trim(ltrim(x,'#')) on both sides of each join.
lines.rank: Quote lines ordered by product name; policy rules ordered by article title then paragraph number, via row_number() within each kind partition (s=1 lines, s=2 rules).
lines.parse: Quantity, UnitPrice, Discount, TotalPrice text fields cast to numeric; faq_answer__c split on blank lines into paragraphs numbered by ordinality, keeping only paragraphs starting with a digit and period (numbered rules).
lines.shape: Single result set unioning quote-line rows (kind, product, quantity, list_price, unit_price, discount, total_price) and policy-rule rows (kind, article_id, title, rule text), ordered s,o.
lines.filter: Restrict quote lines to QuoteId = 0Q0Wt000001WSDVKA4; restrict knowledge articles to those whose summary equals the title or starts with 'Policy'; keep only rule paragraphs that mention no specific product or mention a product present on this quote.
lines.metric: No aggregation - produces a flat listing at the grain of one row per quote line item and one row per kept policy rule paragraph, tagged by kind.
lines.sources: Quote lines from crmarenapro_quotelineitem joined to crmarenapro_product2 (Name) and crmarenapro_pricebookentry (UnitPrice as list price); policy text from crmarenapro_knowledge__kav's faq_answer__c body field, plus summary and title columns.

lines.keys: Task.WhatId matched to Opportunity.Id after stripping leading '#' and trimming whitespace from both sides via ltrim/trim.
lines.rank: Rows ordered first by a synthetic flag (opportunity row before task rows), then by activity_date ascending, then by id; no limit.
lines.parse: Trailing/leading spaces trimmed from Id, Name, StageName, Status, Subject, Description; no JSON or regex extraction, just trim/ltrim of '#' prefix.
lines.shape: Returns columns kind, id, activity_date, status, subject, description as a chronological list mixing the opportunity's stage and its tasks.
lines.filter: Opportunity restricted to the single Id 006Wt000007BGGjIAO (after normalisation); its joined tasks are all included, no status/date filter.
lines.metric: No aggregation; builds a union of one opportunity summary row plus one row per linked task, each row a raw fact for manual reading.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_opportunity gives Id, Name, StageName, CloseDate; crmarenapro_task gives WhatId, ActivityDate, Status, Subject, Description as task detail fields.

lines.keys: Match case.orderitemid__c to orderitem."Id" after stripping/trimming leading '#' and whitespace from both sides via ltrim(trim(x),'#'); orderitem filtered by normalized "Product2Id" equal to the given product id.
lines.rank: Order groups by case count descending, then by month_start ascending as tie-break; no explicit LIMIT applied in the query as written.
lines.parse: Cast case.createddate text (format 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MI:SS.000+0000') to timestamptz, convert to UTC, truncate to month via date_trunc('month', ...) for grouping and formatted with to_char(...,'FMMonth') for display.
lines.shape: Returns rows with two columns: month (formatted month name) and cases (count), one row per month, ordered by highest count first.
lines.filter: Keep only cases whose matched orderitem's Product2Id (normalized) equals the given product id, and whose createddate (as UTC date) falls between today minus 10 months and today inclusive.
lines.metric: Count of cases (count(*)) grouped by calendar month (month_start from date_trunc) to get case volume per month for the product.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case (createddate, orderitemid__c) links to crmarenapro_orderitem ("Id", "Product2Id") to identify SecureAnalytics Pro cases via product id.

lines.keys: orderitem rows filtered to the given Product2Id, then joined to case on orderitemid__c = orderitem Id, both normalised by stripping a leading '#' after trimming whitespace.
lines.rank: Order groups by case count descending; take the single top row (limit 1); no explicit tie-break beyond default ordering.
lines.parse: issueid__c and orderitemid__c/Product2Id/Id are read as plain text and cleaned via ltrim(trim(x),'#') to drop a leading '#' marker; createddate is cast from timestamptz at UTC to a date.
lines.shape: Single row, single column named issue_id containing the most frequent issue's normalised id.
lines.filter: Product2Id must equal the given product id (normalised); case createddate's UTC date must fall within today minus 5 months through today inclusive; issueid__c must not be null.
lines.metric: Count of case rows (not distinct-deduplicated beyond grouping) per normalised issue id, grouped by issue_id, representing frequency of that issue for the product.
lines.sources: Issue text comes from case.issueid__c; product linkage via orderitem table's Id and Product2Id columns; case table gives createddate for the time window.

lines.keys: Line items join to Product2 and PricebookEntry by matching Id after trimming spaces and stripping a leading '#' from each side; quote filter matches QuoteId the same normalised way.
lines.rank: Quote lines are ordered by product name; kept policy rules are ordered by article title then paragraph number; two blocks are concatenated with quote lines first via an outer sequence/row-number ordering, no limit applied.
lines.parse: Numeric-as-text fields (Quantity, UnitPrice, Discount, TotalPrice, pricebook UnitPrice) are cast to numeric; knowledge article body is split into paragraphs on blank lines via regexp_split_to_table, keeping only paragraphs starting with a number and a period as rule text, whitespace collapsed.
lines.shape: Output columns kind, article_id, title, product, quantity, list_price, unit_price, discount, total_price, rule - one row per quote line item and one row per applicable policy rule, for manual comparison rather than a single computed verdict.
lines.filter: Restrict to line items whose normalised QuoteId equals the given quote; restrict candidate knowledge articles to those whose summary equals its title or whose summary starts with 'Policy'; keep only numbered-paragraph rules; drop rules that name a specific catalog product unless that product appears among the quote's line items.
lines.metric: No aggregation is computed; grain is one row per quote line item (with product, quantity, list/unit price, discount, total price) union one row per surviving policy rule paragraph (with article id, title, rule text), tagged by a 'kind' label.
lines.sources: Quote line items come from crmarenapro_quotelineitem (QuoteId, Product2Id, PricebookEntryId, Quantity, UnitPrice, Discount, TotalPrice); product names from crmarenapro_product2.Name; list prices from crmarenapro_pricebookentry.UnitPrice; policy text from crmarenapro_knowledge__kav.faq_answer__c, plus its id and title/summary.

lines.keys: case ids and agent ids matched after normalizing: trim whitespace and strip leading '#' from caseid__c, oldvalue__c, newvalue__c; transfers.agent joined to handled.agent on the normalized id.
lines.rank: order agents by transfer count ascending, tie-broken by agent id ascending, limit to 1 row (the minimum).
lines.parse: createddate text parsed by taking the first 10 characters (left(...,10)) and casting to date to get the UTC calendar day; oldvalue__c/newvalue__c cleaned via trim+ltrim of '#' and blanked-to-null via nullif.
lines.shape: single column output aliased as "Id", one row: the agent id with fewest transfers among those with more than 0 handled cases.
lines.filter: field__c trimmed equals 'Owner Assignment'; createddate day within [lo,hi) window = the four complete quarters before current quarter (2022-04-01 to 2023-03-31); from_agent/to_agent not null where required.
lines.metric: for each agent: handled = count of distinct normalized case_id where they appear as newvalue__c (to_agent) in window; transfers = count of rows where they appear as oldvalue__c (from_agent) in window.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_casehistory__c table, field__c column identifying 'Owner Assignment' rows, oldvalue__c/newvalue__c for agent ids, caseid__c for case, createddate text column for the event date.

lines.keys: Join case.accountid to account.Id after trimming whitespace and stripping leading '#' from both sides, exact match.
lines.rank: Order states by ascending average closure seconds, tie-break alphabetically by state name, limit to 1 row.
lines.parse: createddate read via left(...,10) cast to date to get the date part from the timestamp-like text; closeddate/createddate cast to timestamptz for interval subtraction.
lines.shape: Single column 'state' with one row: the two-letter state abbreviation with quickest average closure time.
lines.filter: Only cases with non-null closeddate; createddate date falls within the 6 complete quarters before current quarter (2021-04-01 to 2022-09-30, exclusive upper bound).
lines.metric: For each state, average closure time in seconds (closeddate - createddate) computed via extract(epoch from ...), grouped by trimmed ShippingState.
lines.sources: crmarenapro_case (createddate, closeddate, accountid) and crmarenapro_account (Id, ShippingState) provide dates/state; state is a plain text field on account.

lines.keys: packageinfo joined to project_packageversion on System='NPM', Name, Version; result joined to project_info on lowercased ProjectName equal to lowercased owner/repo extracted from Project_Information
lines.rank: order by stars descending, tie-broken by Name descending, limited to top 5 rows
lines.parse: Ordinal and IsRelease read from VersionInfo JSONB via ->>; owner/repo repo-slug extracted from Project_Information via regex; star count extracted via first matching regex among 'stars count of N', 'starred by N', 'N stars', commas stripped and cast to bigint
lines.shape: two columns Name and Version, one row per package, 5 rows total
lines.filter: System='NPM', IsRelease true; per package keep only the row with highest Ordinal (rn=1) as the latest release; only rows where a matching project and star count exist
lines.metric: max star count per Name/Version release, grouped by Name and Version, using the single latest version per package
lines.sources: deps_dev_v1_packageinfo (Name, Version, VersionInfo JSON for Ordinal/IsRelease), deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion (System, Name, Version, ProjectName), deps_dev_v1_project_info (Project_Information free text with repo and star count)

lines.keys: project matched by lowercased owner/repo extracted from Project_Information vs lowercased ProjectName; packageinfo joined to project_packageversion on exact System, Name, Version
lines.rank: order all qualifying projects by forks descending, tie-break by ProjectName ascending, limit to 5
lines.parse: regex extracts owner/repo substring from Project_Information; three alternative regexes extract fork counts ('forks count of N', 'forked N times', 'N forks'), commas stripped and cast to bigint; VersionInfo JSON parsed for Ordinal and IsRelease boolean
lines.shape: ProjectName, Version, ForksCount, five rows
lines.filter: Licenses JSON array contains 'MIT'; packageinfo System = 'NPM' and VersionInfo IsRelease true; only projects present in the MIT proj set
lines.metric: per project pick the latest release version (row_number by UpstreamPublishedAt desc, then Ordinal desc, then Version desc, rn=1), pair with the extracted forks count
lines.sources: deps_dev_v1_project_info (Licenses JSON, Project_Information free text for owner/repo and forks); deps_dev_v1_packageinfo (System, Name, Version, VersionInfo JSON, UpstreamPublishedAt); deps_dev_v1_project_packageversion (ProjectName, System, Name, Version)

lines.keys: files.id joined to contents.id (exact blob id match) to get README text; languages.repo_name joined to files.repo_name (exact) restricted to repos with a README.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: path matched case-insensitively for README.md at path start or after a slash; language_description parsed via regex for a 'Python' token followed by '(N bytes' or ', totaling N bytes' patterns.
lines.shape: single row with three columns: total_readmes, copyright_readmes, proportion (float ratio, not rounded).
lines.filter: keep only files whose path is README.md and have a contents row; keep repos whose languages rows exist and none of them match the Python token pattern; join filtered readmes to those non-Python repos.
lines.metric: per matched README row, flag has_copyright as content matching 'copyright' or '©' (case-insensitive); count total readmes and count with the flag, then compute ratio.
lines.sources: github_repos_files (repo_name, path, id) locates README.md files; github_repos_contents.content holds file text keyed by id; github_repos_languages.language_description holds per-repo language sentences.

lines.keys: files.id joins to contents.id (blob id, exact match); files.repo_name joins to languages.repo_name (exact match), restricted to repos already appearing among described Swift files.
lines.rank: order by parsed copies descending, tie-break by repo_name ascending, limit to 1 row.
lines.parse: path filtered by regex matching '.swift' suffix, case-insensitive; from repo_data_description extract the integer preceding the literal word 'times' as copies; languages.language_description matched by regex requiring 'Swift' followed by '(N bytes' or ', totaling N bytes' as a language token.
lines.shape: single row output containing repo_name only (the file's repo_name for the top-copied swift file).
lines.filter: files.path must end in .swift (case-insensitive); contents.repo_data_description must contain the whole word 'non-binary'; languages rows must contain a valid Swift token; repo restricted to those with at least one described swift file.
lines.metric: distinct-on id dedups files to one row per file id (first repo_name/path alphabetically); copies is the parsed integer per file, one value per file id, no aggregation beyond dedup.
lines.sources: github_repos_files gives id, repo_name, path per file; github_repos_contents.repo_data_description (text) gives copy-count phrasing and binary flag; github_repos_languages.language_description lists languages with byte counts per repo_name.

lines.keys: shell_apache_repos derived by joining languages and licenses tables on exact repo_name match; commits joined to that set via repo_name equality.
lines.rank: none
lines.parse: language_description matched via LIKE '%Shell%' substring search within the text field; no JSON parsing; message length via LENGTH(), prefix checked via LOWER() LIKE patterns.
lines.shape: single row with one column total_count, an integer count.
lines.filter: repos require language_description containing 'Shell' and license exactly 'apache-2.0'; commits require message IS NOT NULL, LENGTH(message) < 1000, and lowercased message not starting with 'merge', 'update', or 'test'.
lines.metric: simple count of qualifying commit rows (COUNT(*)), no grouping, each commit counted once.
lines.sources: github_repos_languages.language_description (text list of languages) and github_repos_licenses.license identify repo attributes; github_repos_commits.message holds commit text; all keyed by repo_name.

lines.keys: commits and langs matched on exact repo_name; main and commits joined on exact repo_name via USING clause.
lines.rank: rows ordered by num_commits descending, limited to the top 5, no explicit tie-break beyond that.
lines.parse: main_language extracted from language_description via regex substring capturing the text after 'in' or ':' up to before ' (<digits with commas> bytes' or ', totaling'.
lines.shape: two columns returned: repo_name and num_commits, five rows, though question asks only for repo names.
lines.filter: langs restricted to repo_name present in commits (pre-filtering before regex); final result restricted to rows where extracted main_language is not exactly 'Python'; inner join drops repos with no language row.
lines.metric: num_commits computed per repo_name as count(*) over github_repos_commits rows, one row per repo.
lines.sources: github_repos_commits table (repo_name, one row per commit) for commit counts; github_repos_languages table's language_description text column for the per-repo language breakdown text.

lines.keys: googlelocal_business_description.gmap_id joined to googlelocal_review.gmap_id, an exact key match, no transformation needed.
lines.rank: order by average rating descending, limit to top 5 rows, no explicit tie-break beyond that.
lines.parse: regex extracts the literal phrase 'Los Angeles, CA' or 'Los Angeles, California' as whole words from the description text.
lines.shape: two columns: business name and avg_rating, five rows, values left unrounded as computed by avg().
lines.filter: rows whose description matches the Los Angeles CA/California pattern via word-boundary regex; no date window or other exclusions.
lines.metric: average of review.rating per business (grouped by gmap_id and name), unrounded mean across all matching reviews.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description.description holds templated prose naming city/state/zip; googlelocal_review.rating holds per-review star ratings; business name in .name.

lines.keys: massage CTE's gmap_id joins to googlelocal_review.gmap_id directly; both sides need only the raw gmap_id, no stripping or casing needed.
lines.rank: order the final results by the numeric avg_rating descending; no limit, no tie-break specified beyond that.
lines.parse: name matched case-insensitively against '\mmassage' word boundary; description matched against a regex alternation of bodywork, body treatment(s), therap(y/ies/ist/ists/eutic), massag phrasings.
lines.shape: two columns: name and avg_rating rounded to 15 decimal places cast to text (to preserve trailing zeros/decimal point), one row per qualifying business.
lines.filter: rows where name or description regex matches count as massage businesses; then after grouping, only keep groups whose average rating is >= 4.0.
lines.metric: per business (grouped by gmap_id, name) compute the average of r.rating across all joined reviews, giving one avg_rating per business.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description table holds gmap_id, name, and description text for massage detection; googlelocal_review table holds rating and gmap_id for scoring.

lines.keys: Businesses matched to reviews by exact gmap_id equality; hours JSON exploded per business via gmap_id before joining to review ratings by the same gmap_id.
lines.rank: Ordered by avg_rating descending, then by n_reviews ascending, then by name ascending as tie-breakers, limited to top 5 rows.
lines.parse: hours cast to jsonb and expanded into (day, hrs) pairs with ordinality; hrs matched by regex extracting open hour/minute/AM-PM and close hour/minute/AM-PM around an en dash, converting each to minutes since midnight (12-hour to 24-hour, minutes optional, open AM/PM inferred from close if omitted).
lines.shape: Five rows with columns name, operating_hours (JSON-like string of day/hours pairs), and avg_rating.
lines.filter: Only rows with non-null hours are parsed; only Monday-Friday entries considered; a business qualifies if any weekday entry is 'Open 24 hours', has close_min > 18:00, or close_min <= open_min (wraps past midnight); exact 6PM close excluded.
lines.metric: Per gmap_id: average of review.rating (avg_rating) and count of reviews (n_reviews), computed only for businesses passing the evening-open filter; hours text rebuilt as a concatenated JSON-like string of [day, hrs] pairs in original order.
lines.sources: googlelocal_business_description.hours (JSON array of [day, hours] pairs) for schedules; googlelocal_review.rating for ratings; googlelocal_business_description.name/gmap_id for identity.

lines.keys: reviews.gmap_id matches business_description.gmap_id exactly, an inner join with no transformation needed on either side.
lines.rank: order by review count descending, ties broken alphabetically by business name, limited to top 3.
lines.parse: time text is matched by regex to detect which of three formats it is, then parsed with to_timestamp using the matching format string (ISO, 'DD Mon YYYY, HH24:MI', or 'FMMonth DD, YYYY at HH12:MI AM').
lines.shape: two columns: business name and high_rating_count, three rows, one per top business.
lines.filter: rating >= … (only 5-star reviews qualify since rating is integer), and parsed timestamp falls within 2019-01-01 inclusive to 2020-01-01 exclusive.
lines.metric: count of qualifying reviews grouped per business (by gmap_id and name), one count per business.
lines.sources: googlelocal_review holds gmap_id, rating, and time (text in three different formats); googlelocal_business_description holds gmap_id and name.

lines.keys: tracks and sales matched on track_id after tracks are reduced to matching song_records; each track's song/performer text unwrapped per its source_id format before matching.
lines.rank: none - no ordering or limiting, single aggregate result.
lines.parse: song and performer extracted from title per source_id: strip ' (Album)' or trailing parenthetical for source 1, split 'Artist - Title' or 'Title - Album' on ' - ' for sources 2/3, strip leading 3-4 digit code for source 4, else title as-is; then lower-cased, accents translated to plain letters, and non-alphanumeric characters stripped for both song and artist.
lines.shape: one row, one column revenue_usd, rounded to 2 decimal places.
lines.filter: only tracks whose folded song_key and artist_key are within one character deletion (either side) of the folded 'getmebodied'/'beyonce' keys; then sales rows restricted to store = Apple Music and country = Canada.
lines.metric: sum of revenue_usd across all matched sales rows for the matched duplicate track records, i.e. total revenue for the song grain not per-record.
lines.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks holds title/album/artist text per track_id and source_id; music_brainz_20k_sales holds revenue_usd, store, country per track_id.

lines.keys: tracks and sales joined on track_id, an exact key; track_id resolved via matching to candidate track rows first.
lines.rank: order stores by summed revenue_usd descending, take top 1 row, ties broken by arbitrary order.
lines.parse: title and artist stripped of all non-letters and lowercased via regexp_replace, comparing letters-only forms; surname taken as second word of 'Brucqe Maginnis' split on space, also letters-only lowered.
lines.shape: single column 'store', one row, the top-earning store, no rounding applied.
lines.filter: track rows where cleaned title contains 'streethype' and cleaned artist contains cleaned surname 'maginnis'; no date window or other exclusions.
lines.metric: sum of sales.revenue_usd grouped by store, aggregating across all matched track_id rows and all countries.
lines.sources: music_brainz_20k_tracks (title, artist columns) for song identity; music_brainz_20k_sales (store, revenue_usd) for revenue.

lines.keys: tracks join sales on track_id; duplicate tracks of the same song are linked via computed song_key/artist_key rather than any stored key.
lines.rank: order clusters by summed revenue_usd descending, take the single top cluster (limit 1).
lines.parse: per source_id, strip album suffix ' (Album)', split 'Artist - Title', split 'Title - Album', strip leading 'NNN-' digits from title; extract performer similarly for source 2; then lower-case, fold accents, strip non-alphanumerics to get song_key and artist_key.
lines.shape: list the title column from all track_id records belonging to the winning cluster, ordered by track_id ascending, no other columns.
lines.filter: drop records with empty song_key or artist_key, or artist_key equal to 'unknown'; only link keys of length 6+ via one-character-deletion variants for typo tolerance.
lines.metric: for each track, generate one-deletion variants of song_key and artist_key, join on exact artist+variant or title+variant matches to build edges, propagate minimum track_id label across three rounds to cluster duplicate records, then sum revenue_usd per cluster.

lines.keys: patients.barcode (extracted TCGA-XX-XXXX substring) joined to rnaseq r.ParticipantBarcode on exact match, combined with r.Symbol = 'IGF2'.
lines.rank: Results ordered alphabetically by Histology_Type; no row limit or top-N.
lines.parse: Barcode read via regex TCGA-[A-Z0-9]{2}-[A-Z0-9]{4}; disease name read via coalesce of three regex patterns matching 'case of/subject with/diagnosed with/study of X,' or 'belongs to the X cohort.' or 'In the X dataset,'.
lines.shape: Two columns: Histology_Type and Average_Log_Expression, one row per histology code, numeric average with at least four decimal places.
lines.filter: disease = 'Brain lower grade glioma'; icd_o_3_histology not null and not matching bracketed pattern ^\[.*\]$; r.normalized_count not null and > -1 (valid for log).

lines.keys: Join extracted barcode from Patient_description to ParticipantBarcode in mutation data; needs exact TCGA barcode extracted, no case folding needed.

lines.rank: none

lines.keys: yelp_business.business_id matched to yelp_review.business_ref by stripping 'businessid_' prefix and replacing with 'businessref_'.

lines.metric: Count distinct business_id per parsed category to find business count per category; then average yelp_review.rating (cast to float) across all reviews of businesses in the top category.

lines.rank: States ordered by business count descending, ties broken alphabetically by state code, limited to 1 (top state).
